title: Seven at the Teeth

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: Seven times a word may come to the teeth and go back, and seven times is a keeping and not a payment. A reed bundle is counted in the arm that carried it, and a year held to its last day is a year still held. What is held is owed, and what is owed waits for a hand that has not come.
epigraph.attribution: A proverb of Low Kiln, said over the banked fire in the last tend of Reed

where: Low Kiln, the Weir and Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-forty-one-to-one-hundred-and-forty-three-day-old body carried everywhere; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (a carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, a further shaping of two absences named in one breath as an appetite, a sentence stopped at the word as an object on the interval tray, a hand under a board that knows it by heart or was told not to look, the dark foot read exactly and worth nothing) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room, back-room interior, Ulda on stage, Fenna named in narration, a seventh hearing, a sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, a sixth green, a calling of the loan, a spending of the seventh year or an ending

scenes.title: The Last Week's Bundles
scenes.synopsis: First entry and first dated heading of Day 141, Reed 22, Secondday, morning going into midday at the Clay Yard and the reed beds below Low Kiln. The reed month goes into its last week; the boy is one hundred and forty-one days old and four months and twenty-one days and nobody under any roof says so. Sella Vail carries him at the half-pace she keeps from every open slate and gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket (T058/T079). The week's last bundles come downriver and go back in armfuls judged by the arm that carries them; a cutter tells a girl with a creel that her arm knows what went into a bundle and that is the whole of what it knows, and an arm asking cost is answered with the weather and the river, never a figure (T071/T072, T077). The yard goes around the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out --- a look, a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried, not paid). The reed-cutter's grey cord goes past along the boards unread, straightened and turned where no slate lies (T099 carried, not paid). The boy reads the carrying arm once more as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost: exact, complete and worth nothing, and notes the order in which the reaching hand goes to the record before the person without having standing to enter it anywhere (T061/T082). Advances T071/T072 (141 kept exact and unspent), T077, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T098, T099, T061/T082. Withheld: no figure for the hands or the reeds, no knot counted, no name, cause, body or count for the missing hand, no joining of the empty places.

scenes.title: One Appetite, Two Rooms
scenes.synopsis: Second entry continued, Day 141, midday into the afternoon under the Vail kiln-house roof at the loaf shelf and the hearth. Sella sets the basket low near the bench leg at the angle at which the underside of a board becomes a roof, gives the instruction to the wool, the pot, the broom and the fire and never to the basket, and tells the fire it was the thaw (T058/T079). Above, the shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps --- the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6 with no scrape, crumb, print or word --- in a room the fold does not touch (T060/T086). A neighbour at the shelf reaches past the bare board, her hand going to it before her eyes go to the boy, and names the old gap as a thing the planting brought in and the empty place at his ear as a child's appetite under one appetite in a single breath: a further shaping of T097 held beside the earlier tellings on a place of its own, advanced and not paid, with no third gap, no finger laid, no joining, no name and no fourth likeness made into a cause (T097, T060/T086). Sella moves her lips along the row, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze, gives nobody a figure, and sends the neighbour to the pot with *Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it* (T077). Standing with her back to the basket, she reaches a finger BENEATH the front edge where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, and brings it away and does not go back to the shelf (T100 carried, unread). The boy sees the hand go under and come back and sees nothing of what the marks say; such a hand either knows the board by heart or has been told not to look, and the reason stands between the two. The widow's mark is untouched, because a shelf and an afternoon are not openings (T079). He keeps one brown-edged crust in the fold and two gaps in the other room and does not let the rooms touch. Advances T097 (further shaping, not paid), T100 (carried), T060/T086, T058/T079, T077, T079. Withheld hard: no stroke counted, no figure read, no copying hand, no joining of the charcoal to the two gaps above or to the crust in the fold.

scenes.title: Six Where the House Can Check
scenes.synopsis: Third entry and first dated heading of Day 142, Reed 23, Thirdday, Y.H. 813, before first grey through midday at the Vail wheel-shed, its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the cold damper, the Clay Yard and the flagstones. Three or four unnamed men come up with their collars high and go low-voiced into the room off the shed; Sella carries the boy past at the half-pace, gives the house no name for the men and does not say the room was cold (T035/T031). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack are entered by nobody (T035/T031, T009/T013/T092). He speaks to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*), tells a pot *You'll do*, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master who would call it early and make something of it (T062). Before Sella has finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper, moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves it standing; the boy reads the iron again as the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that can take the hand off a man, with no Grathic word for both mercies, filed as an object joined to no kiln (T062). The two tellings of the shut counting room stay together with no third (T065/T095 carried). Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed; his seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood, the small knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 still unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach (T036/T076). His stroke goes on over the flagstones without the half-check and the stones keep the shallow bright patch where it stopped; neither man asks about the ear or the room and the two silences stay unjoined. Advances T035/T031, T062, T065/T095, T036/T076, T009/T013/T092, T058/T079, T061/T082, T071/T072 (142 kept exact). Withheld: no naming of the men, no entry of the room, no third telling, no calling word, no spending of the seventh year.

scenes.title: Seven at the Teeth
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry continued, Day 142, afternoon at the Cross and the market stalls, below the north bridge, then the going of the light into the small hours at the hearth and kindling under the Vail roof. Berr Clay appears briefly: he comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded under his coat and the green of tasted glaze at one corner of his mouth, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened against his forearm, passes a finger over the figure and reads *one in twelve, as the notice says* low, calls the levy and denies it with *your house*, never *I*, says *A number goes into a slate, not a bundle*, pays two marks short for eels which the stall-keeper puts in her palm without counting where anyone can hear, and goes off up the road with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done the district a kindness (T015/T041/T047/T077). A figure read aloud is not the figure paid. Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing, slate to his forearm with the writing inward, hand to slate before eyes to stalls (T090/T080/T083). Under the roof, with the coals banked and the small knife set back where it could be checked, Tarn tells the kindling *Six counted. The next I don't count* and brings the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it all the way to the word that would call the loan a SEVENTH time --- after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20 --- and stops there with no figure and no name; he draws the breath that should have gone in at the top of the reach and does not spend it, says *Yes, house* to the fire and goes on with the broom (T036/T076). The chapter's one meaningful change: the boy files the seventh stopping on the interval tray beside the six as a SEVENTH INTERVAL AND NOT A SEVENTH PAYMENT, an object among objects and not a rule, not a hearing and not a seventh hearing, refusing to let seven likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine --- for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer --- with no payer named to any of the seven (T036/T076, T061/T082). Sella, within hearing, gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and Tarn does not ask about the room, and the two silences stay unjoined. The seventh year stands one tend from its end and has not given; the loan stays uncalled; the carried fire keeps four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been with its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-two days (T088). Advances T015/T041/T047, T090/T080/T083, T036/T076, T061/T082, T088, T058/T079. Withheld hard: no calling of the loan, no spending of the Seed 16 breath, no cutting or counting of the seventh year, no collector, no payer, no seventh hearing, no sixth green.

scenes.title: Neither Knot Counted
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry and first dated heading of Day 143, Reed 24, Fourthday, Y.H. 813, morning going into midday downriver at the Weir, the plank walk on posts, the flat blessing stone and the lower boards, then below the sill at the fish-trade shade. The reed-cutter comes along the boards with a bundle and the short length of grey wool or reed-fibre cord gone grey with the oil of a working thumb; he straightens it on the flat stone, turns it once so the knots stand, ties one low with his teeth and a pull of the thumb, bites the end off and puts it back inside his coat, answering a woman who cannot read it with *You can ask the cord* and *No more can the Court*; no figure, knot, name or joining, and no laying of it beside the missing hand, Mira's cords or Orra's knot-string (T099 carried, not paid). Orra Weir stands at the lower boards with her board on its side and her hands like old rope, pale eel scars uncovered, salt white at her wrists, and pulls one knot down with her thumb, giving a date where a figure was asked --- the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat round the bend on the flood with six oars and one man at the stern who never touched them --- and keeping the word forty unspoken with the forty-first double turn legible and unnamed (T024). Mira Silt works the eels with pale slime dried in long grey strokes on her sleeves and silt pale in the hollow of her neck, her head held a little right where the top of her left ear had been, her small smile kept like a door on the latch; asked whether the run will be thin she answers her own answer, *Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river*, flicks eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie and puts one away. When a buyer names a figure her thumb goes under her apron to the grey cord and stays longer than the figure required; the second cord twisted twice beneath it is never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the thin child's knot untouched, her board beside Orra's and not touching (T059/T025/T024). Below the sill the child's foot stays dark inside three turns of wool, the cold to the woman who wrapped it and weather to the yard and a neighbour with a pail; the surgeon's reading of the extremity going before the core and the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform works perfectly and buys nothing, with no silt-leach, cause, cure or recognition written across it (T093/T094/T096). The soft-cuffed clerk is still set at the landing for the uncalled measure (T090/T080). Sella sets the basket at the edge of the work where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket (T058/T079). Advances T099, T024/T059/T025, T093/T094/T096, T090/T080, T058/T079, T071/T072 (143 kept exact). Withheld: no knot counted, no figure read, no word forty, no silt-leach, cause or cure, no joining of the cord to the missing hand or to any other private record.

scenes.title: The Last Bundles Stand
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry continued, Day 143, afternoon at the Clay Yard and the reed beds and under the Vail kiln-house roof at the loaf shelf. The reed bundles stand grey in the ruts with nobody counting them, green at the broken ends and pale at the frost-bitten tips, the reed month in its last week and the third Account-day of Reed (Reed 30, Day 149) six days off; a cutter judges an armful by the arm that carried it, and a woman who asks what the hands will be paid is answered with the weather and the river, never a figure (T071/T072, T077, T058/T079). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Sella sets the basket low at the loaf-shelf angle; a neighbour with a wet pot asks what the row will want before the tend is out and is sent to the pot with *The house has said it*, carrying the unanswered question away level (T077). Standing with her back to the basket and moving her lips along the row with its two unnamed gaps, she reaches a finger beneath the front edge where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, and brings it away and does not go back to the shelf (T100 carried, unread). The boy sees the hand go under and come back, makes no cause of the habit and does not lay the charcoal under the shelf across the two gaps above or the one stiff crust in the fold; the two rooms do not touch and no third gap comes (T100, T060/T086, T097). The widow's mark hangs where it hangs, untouched at a shelf and an afternoon, because neither is an opening; the clean dark line and the finer grey stay unswept and are called the thaw (T079, T009/T013/T092). Advances T100 (carried), T071/T072 (143 exact), T077, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T098, T060/T086, T097. Withheld: no stroke counted, no figure read, no name, body or count for the missing hand, no joining of the absences.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Forty-Three
scenes.synopsis: Seventh entry continued, Day 143, the going of the light into the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof at the bed, the hearth and the loaf shelf seen from the basket's low angle. Sella carries him up the clay road at the half-pace from every open slate, goes around a pan set out to dry and the trough by the well with its skin of ice, goes wide around the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting before it goes away; she tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes a strand of coal-black hair back with the wrist that carries the little-door burn, the grey streak pale, sets the pot rim out with the handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and neither looks toward the bed nor touches the widow's mark, because a dusk is not an opening (T058/T079, T079). In the small hours he turns out his file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh; three near-full answers advanced and not paid; the older intervals with the half-beat behind the standing finger, the stroke that went on without the check and his own held breath; SEVEN stoppings of the near-saying as objects and not a rule, intervals and not payments, no payer named to any, with the seventh year standing one tend from its end and still held; the damper's double bite filed joined to no kiln; the two shut-room tellings with no third; the told bell beside the heard bell (T061/T082, T036/T076, T062, T065/T095, T078). In the other room the loaf shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps and the charcoal under the board stays unread; one crust lies stiff in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third; the word forty stays unspoken with the readable double turn beside it; the fifth green stays a colour and not a name joined to no ear; the reed-cutter's cord, Mira's second twist and Orra's knot-string stay unread; Alda's six pages and both tins and Dessa's pewter tin stay shut; the clerk stays set for an uncalled measure; the cold foot stays the cold to one woman and weather to the yard (T100, T060/T086, T097, T098, T099, T024/T059/T025, T050/T051, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T096). Through the finger's-width door comes the river's note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; through the floor under blind ash the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-three days; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a fifth that is a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places and none becomes one (T088, T061/T082). Cold arrives cheek, temple, wrist, the wool riding back from the small bare joint. One hundred and forty-three days old and four months and twenty-three days, told by nobody, and if somebody said the number under that roof nobody would know what it counted. His hand goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold, exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody; in the next room the charcoal waits under the shelf for a hand not his and a day that has not come. Advances T071/T072 (143 exact, unspent), T061/T082, T036/T076 (seventh stopping filed as object not payment, loan uncalled), T088, T058/T079, T060/T086, T097, T098, T099, T100, T024/T059/T025, T050/T051, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T096, T009/T013/T092, T062, T065/T095, T078. Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called, spent or ended; no seventh hearing, no sixth green, no sixth sighting, no sale and no ending.
